data.image_selection: first num_images images of the CIFAR10 test split in dataset order (deterministic -- shuffle=False, no DataLoader generator randomness)
data.normalization: standard CIFAR10 mean/std (src/utility/utils.py _norm); no augmentation (test transform: Resize -> ToTensor -> Normalize only, RandomCrop/Flip excluded)

estimator.probe_seed_reset: torch.manual_seed(probe_seed) immediately before every estimator call

basis.note: PTQ/QAT exist only fused+quantized, so fused is canonical for any PTQ/QAT comparison. FP32 is still traced in BOTH bases (fp32_unfused, fp32_fused) and the unfused->fused fusion_ratio is always reported alongside FP32 so nothing is hidden by the basis choice (see src/analysis/quant_induced_trace.py).

CIFAR10.note: original frozen CIFAR10 config (relock_traces.py Part 0) -- referenced here, not duplicated logic; top-level keys are the source of truth and are unchanged by this extension.

IMAGENET100.normalization: standard IMAGENET100 mean/std (src/utility/utils.py _norm); val transform only (Resize(256) -> CenterCrop(224) -> ToTensor -> Normalize, no augmentation)
IMAGENET100.note: probe count (max_iter=30) and image count (24) reduced from CIFAR10's (max_iter=100, num_images=80) -- 224x224 HVP cost is far higher per iteration than 32x32; this is a recorded cross-dataset difference (spike_layer_cause.py Part 0), not a silent one. Matched WITHIN IMAGENET100 across every model/variant in this module -- spike_layer_cause.py's cross-dataset comparisons (Part 6) use ratios/residuals, not raw trace magnitudes, precisely because of this difference.
